issues.description: The UML in the problem statement declares Farm.addAnimal(animal: Animal): boolean, but the reference implementation uses a void addAnimal(Animal) (and the template does not provide an addAnimal implementation). This mismatch between the UML return type and the actual/expected method signature can confuse students about whether they should return a boolean and how to use the method.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the UML and templates consistent: either change the UML in problem_statement.md to show addAnimal(animal: Animal): void, or change the template and solution to implement addAnimal returning boolean (and update the tasks and examples accordingly). Preferably update the UML to void to match the template/example usage.

issues.description: The helper method singFarmSongVerse is specified in the UML/problem as singFarmSongVerse(animal: Animal): void and the solution implements private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal), but the template's stub defines singFarmSongVerse without an Animal parameter (commented parameter). This parameter mismatch between template and the specification/solution may lead students to incorrectly implement or overload the method, causing compilation or behavior confusion.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template Farm.java method signature to include the Animal parameter (private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal) { ... }) and adjust the stub body accordingly, matching the UML and the solution. Alternatively, if the intention was different, update the UML and solution to match the template.
